title: Choose the look for Fieldnotes
question: The roll assigned the Practical Notebook. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Practical Notebook
options.lineage: The biology practical copy: ruled writing page facing a plain diagram page, marked in red by the teacher
options.thesis: Every slide becomes a practical-copy spread: the lecturer's figure on the plain page, its explanation on the ruled page, your answers marked in the margin.
options.viewport: Opens on the next unread slide: the figure large on the plain page, the explanation on the ruled page, a numbered slide strip on top, one green Next in the margin bar.
options.risk: Ruling can turn into costume; it must organise the page (margin column, rules as dividers), never sit behind the text.

raised.raise: Regions never move: figure, explanation and action bar hold their places; changing slides swaps contents only.
One commit colour: forest green is spent only on the single action that moves you forward.
A slide strip always shows where you are: read slides filled, the current one outlined.
Every size and gap comes from one fixed grid; nothing sits off it.
The stage is always marked: Read, Recall, Practise, with missed items as the way back.
No state rides on colour alone: every mark is a word plus a shape (✓ Correct, ✕ Not quite).

options.label: Lecture Handout
options.lineage: PowerPoint 'Handouts, 3 slides per page', photocopied before every exam
options.thesis: The lecture as the handout students already print: each slide beside a lined note column, three to a sheet.
options.viewport: A scrolling handout: every slide with its explanation in the lined column beside it; you scroll the lecture like flipping printed sheets.
options.risk: Closest to today's split layout and to what most study apps ship: familiar more than distinctive.

options.label: PC-98 Sixteen-Colour Screen
options.thesis: Fixed screen regions, a text window docked low, artwork owning the frame.
options.viewport: The slide as the artwork, the explanation in a docked text window.
options.case: Fuses poorly: students don't read biology through retro game screens, and bitmap type hurts long reading.

options.label: Creator Hardware Bench
options.lineage: desk instruments with keycaps, knobs and one orange key
options.thesis: Every function a physical key; one orange key commits.
options.viewport: A key grid of lecture functions with an amber status screen.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a hardware panel says 'tool', not 'lecture', and leaves the slide no room.

options.label: Drum Machine Step Row
options.thesis: A row of step keys with a chase light that always shows where now is.
options.viewport: The lecture's slides as a lit step row.
options.case: Fuses in one place only: the step row maps to slides, but the machine world has nothing to do with biology.
options.kept: A strip that always shows where you are.

options.label: CRT Arcade Screen
options.thesis: Fat pixels, scanlines and palette laws on a strict tile grid.
options.viewport: A tile-grid lecture screen with glowing score type.
options.case: Fuses poorly: glow and scanlines fight small slide text.
options.kept: Every size from one fixed grid.

options.label: Mesophotic Deep Dive
options.lineage: technical dives down a reef wall
options.thesis: Descend through stages; one band marks the active depth.
options.viewport: The lecture as a descent with depth markers.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the dive metaphor needs explaining before anyone can study.
options.kept: The current stage is always marked.

options.label: Cyclorama Dawn
options.lineage: theatre lighting on a curved backdrop
options.thesis: Labelled light phases, never colour alone.
options.viewport: Horizon bands carrying each lecture phase.
options.case: Fuses poorly: atmosphere over information, nothing to read.
options.kept: No state carried by colour alone.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean study app in forest green: top bar, lecture grid, reader, flashcards, quiz.
canonCard.viewport: Top bar with a lecture switcher, a reader with slide and notes, familiar quiz cards.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other study app, by design.
